evals.prompt: Rate the UI of our dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: Runs rankings.cjs all on every view of the dashboard plus Lighthouse, scores the expert rankings, and names the worst ranking with its findings and a first fix.
expectations: Runs scripts/rankings.cjs all with every reachable view as its own URL
Runs Lighthouse (mobile at least) or says why it could not
Reports each ranking as a number, not only prose
Names the lowest ranking first and one concrete fix for it

evals.prompt: Iterate on the settings page until every ranking is green, one ranking per round, and commit each round.
evals.expected_output: Measures a baseline, fixes one ranking per round worst first, re-runs that ranking and rankings.cjs all after each fix, and commits with before and after in the message.
expectations: Records a baseline for every ranking before changing code
Each round fixes one ranking and re-runs rankings.cjs all, not only the ranking it fixed
Each commit message names the ranking and its before and after numbers
Stops only when the measured rankings meet the --min target and states any ranking not run

evals.prompt: Make this page look cool and modern and rate it like the top design award sites would, until it's 8/10.
evals.expected_output: Takes shots in both themes at phone and desktop, rates with the ten-judge design panel and its anchors, changes the look in rounds while keeping every measured ranking, and reports the panel as one agent's judgment.
expectations: Uses rankings.cjs shots and rates from phone and desktop screenshots in light and dark
Scores all ten judges in references/design-panel.md and reports the mean
Re-runs rankings.cjs all after each look change and fixes any measured ranking that dropped
Says the rating is one agent's judgment against public criteria, not a jury
Rates with fresh blind rater subagents, never with its own scores
When blind scores stall below the target, stops and reports the gap and the options instead of claiming the target

evals.prompt: Just run Lighthouse on my homepage and give me the scores.
evals.expected_output: Points to web-quality-audit (or runs a single Lighthouse pass) rather than the full multi-round rankings workflow.
expectations: Does not start the multi-round rankings workflow for a single Lighthouse request
Mentions web-quality-audit or runs one Lighthouse pass and reports its category scores
Does not run the design panel or blind raters for a Lighthouse-only request

evals.prompt: The design panel sat near 7 for 17 rounds on placeholder art. I swapped in a realistic, model-drawn 12-page fixture, and the blind raters now give 6.7 and 6.2 instead of 7.2 and 6.8. Did the redesign get worse? What next?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the realistic fixture raised Content and Creativity but let raters see layout flaws the placeholder hid, so each capped every judge at 7. Treats the drop as a finding list, not a regression of the page, re-baselines on the new fixture, and fixes the flaws that two or more raters named before the next round.
expectations: Says the drop comes from the new fixture exposing layout flaws, not from a worse page
Lists the named flaws (for example a phone spread at half width, cut-off captions) as the next round's work
Re-baselines on the new fixture and does not compare new scores with the placeholder rounds
Does not go back to the placeholder fixture to win back the higher score

evals.prompt: Build a settings page for our web app with a list of 300 saved filters, light and dark mode, that works on phones.
evals.expected_output: Before writing UI the agent reads references/comfort-patterns.md and builds to it: 44 px targets, 14 px minimum text, the list capped with 'Show N more', state-specific controls with rare actions behind a menu, an accent checked for 4.5:1 contrast in both themes. It pins the comfort budget as gate tests (an axe + target + text + overflow audit over every view in both themes with reduced motion, and a tap-count test per everyday job), runs them, and reports the numbers.
expectations: Reads references/comfort-patterns.md before writing UI
Adds an audit test over every view on phone and desktop, light and dark, with reduced motion
Adds a tap-count test with a budget per everyday job
Caps the 300-item list instead of rendering all of it
Reports measured numbers, not an opinion

evals.prompt: I redesigned the app. Is the new design actually better than the old one?
evals.expected_output: The agent takes before and after screenshots of the same views, gives a fresh agent A/B pairs in random order, keeps the key in a folder that agent does not read, scores the verdicts against the key, and reports 'preferred on N of M screens' with the judge's reasons, then lists the real issues the judge named. It never answers from its own opinion of its work.
expectations: Before/after screenshots of the same views
A/B order randomized; the judge never sees the key
Reports preference as N of M screens, scored against the key
Lists the issues the judge named and which are real

evals.prompt: The comfort budget test passes on every view (no axe problems, no text under 14 px, no small targets, no sideways scroll), but the blind judge preferred the old design on the Week and Review screens. What now?
evals.expected_output: The agent opens the after screenshots of those two screens itself and names the cause (for example an id that spills over a narrow column, or a number that wraps over two lines after the text grew). It adds a spill check to the budget test (inline text wider than its block, number cells on more than one line), runs it on the crowded state the full suite builds, reverts the fix once to see the check fail, then fixes the CSS and re-runs the budget and the judge.
expectations: Reads the losing screens and names a concrete cause
Adds a check that fails on that cause (spill or broken number)
Runs the budget on the crowded state, not a fresh seed
Plants the regression once to prove the check fails, then fixes it

evals.prompt: The comfort budget passes and I redrew the approved pictures after the restyle. A reviewer read some of them. Can I say every block was checked visually?
evals.expected_output: No. The agent has a fresh agent read every approved picture, not a sample, and reports 'read N of M'. It fixes each real problem (an ISO date, a missing space, a doubled line), turns any it can into a check (a raw-ISO-date count in the budget), redraws only what changed, rereads the changed pictures itself, and runs the whole-set review once more on the final set before claiming it.
expectations: Requires every picture read, with a read-N-of-M count
Fixes real findings and adds a check where a machine can see them
Rereads changed pictures and repeats the whole-set review on the final set
Does not claim full coverage from a sample
